## Can these estimators recover treatment effects when one event can pre-empt the other?

Event 1 (E1) and event 2 (E2) are generated from Weibull
distributions via joint hazards (Beyersmann 2009). Seven scenarios vary
*where* the treatment acts — on E1, E2, or both, as an average
effect (ATE) or heterogeneous one (HTE):

| Scenario | Treatment effect |
|---|---|
| 1 | ATE on E1 only |
| 2 | ATE on E2 only |
| 3 | HTE on E1, no ATE on E2 |
| 4 | HTE on E1, ATE on E2 |
| 5 | HTE on E2, no ATE on E1 |
| 6 | HTE on E2, ATE on E1 |
| 7 | HTE on both |

Scenarios 2, 5 and 6 are the interesting ones: the treatment moves
event 2, so a naive analysis of event 1 alone can show an apparent
effect that is really just a change in who survives long enough to have one.
Fixed at **n = 500**, censoring **on/off**, **500 runs**, horizon = 28. Full
design in `competing_risk/README.md`.

Covariates are drawn from a Gaussian copula at two latent correlations,
**ρ = 0.5** (X1, X2, X3 and the noise X4, X5, X01–X03 correlated: the primary
analysis, and every section below except "Sensitivity analysis") and
**ρ = 0** (independent: the sensitivity analysis). τ(x) is the same function
at both; the runs share their seeds, so that section compares the two ρ with
paired per-run differences.

**Five estimator frameworks**, several shipping in multiple arms that vary
how their pseudo-values/nuisances are built (see `README.md`'s
"Crossfitting" section for the full rationale):

| Family | Arms | Targets |
|---|---|---|
| `ipw` | causal forest on IPW-transformed RMST | cause-specific RMST |
| `csf_cs` | causal survival forest, competing events censored | cause-specific RMST |
| `csf_sh` | causal survival forest, competing events kept in the risk set (Fine-Gray) | subdistribution RMST |
| CF on PV | `whole_oob`, `whole_scf`, `cvps_scf` | RMTL |
| DR: RF on PV | `whole_oob`, `whole_scf`, `cvps_scf` | RMTL |
| T: SL on PV | `whole`, `cvps`, `split` | RMTL |
| DR: SL on PV | `whole`, `cvps` | RMTL |
| DR: RSF on (Y, D) | `oob`, `scf` | RMTL |

The DR families differ only in the per-arm outcome model: a regression of the
pseudo-values (PV) on X, or a competing-risks random survival forest on the
observed (Y, D). All three use whole-sample jackknife pseudo-values in the DR
correction term.

**The truth column depends on the family**: `ipw`/`csf_cs` remove competing
events and target the cause-specific (net) RMST; `csf_sh` keeps them in the
risk set and targets the subdistribution RMST; every pseudo-value family
targets RMTL. `surv_metrics.R` already resolves this per row, so `bias`/
`mse`/etc. below are always scored against the correct truth.

**Scenario 5 flips the sign of the `RMTL1` correlation — expect it, it is
not a bug.** `tau_RMST1_cs` is flat in scenario 5 (no cause-specific effect
on event 1 at all), so every bit of `RMTL1` heterogeneity there is the
competing-risk artefact induced by the (near-mirror-image) `RMTL2`
heterogeneity. An estimator that tracks the real signal correctly therefore
lands *anti-correlated* with the induced `RMTL1` estimand. A consequence:
`tau_RMST1_cs` has zero variance in scenario 5, so `corr`/`spearman`/
`c_stat` are genuine `NA` for the `ipw`/`csf_cs` Event 1 cells there — dropped
by `na.rm = TRUE` below, not treated as 0. See `competing_risk/README.md`
for the full argument.

```{r data}
res_path <- file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "competing_risk")
metrics <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "surv_metrics.RDS"))
figdir <- file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "all_figures", "competing_risk")
dir.create(figdir, showWarnings = F)
# display order and labels - no shared label-dictionary script for this study
# (unlike crossfitting/cf_metrics.R), so these stay inline, matching
# the (retired) sample_size/continuous/cts_results.qmd's precedent
scenario_labels <- c(
  `1` = "ATE E1",
  `2` = "ATE E2",
  `3` = "HTE E1",
  `4` = "HTE E1, ATE E2",
  `5` = "HTE E2",
  `6` = "HTE E2, ATE E1",
  `7` = "HTE E1&2"
)

# framework is split into family (the estimator) and variant (the arm),
# mirroring crossfitting/cf_results.qmd's family/variant split - keeps
# facets legible instead of one flat 16-level factor
framework_family <- c(
  ipw = "IPW",
  csf_cs = "CSF (cause-specific)",
  csf_sh = "Augmented CSF",
  pseudo_cf_whole_oob = "CF on PV",
  pseudo_cf_whole_scf = "CF on PV",
  pseudo_cf_cvps_scf = "CF on PV",
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob = "DR: RF on PV",
  pseudo_dr_whole_scf = "DR: RF on PV",
  pseudo_dr_cvps_scf = "DR: RF on PV",
  sl_t_whole = "T: SL on PV",
  sl_t_cvps = "T: SL on PV",
  sl_t_split = "T: SL on PV",
  sl_dr_whole = "DR: SL on PV",
  sl_dr_cvps = "DR: SL on PV",
  # the outcome model is the RSF on (Y, D), not a regression on pseudo-values;
  # pseudo-values enter the DR correction term only
  rsf_dr_oob = "DR: RSF on (Y, D)",
  rsf_dr_scf = "DR: RSF on (Y, D)",
  # semi-oracles: the production arm's outcome models, true propensity 0.5
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob_semi = "DR: RF on PV",
  sl_dr_whole_semi = "DR: SL on PV",
  rsf_dr_oob_semi = "DR: RSF on (Y, D)"
)
family_levels <- c(
  "IPW",
  "CSF (cause-specific)",
  "Augmented CSF",
  "CF on PV",
  "DR: RF on PV",
  "DR: RSF on (Y, D)",
  "T: SL on PV",
  "DR: SL on PV"
)

framework_variant <- c(
  ipw = "single",
  csf_cs = "single",
  csf_sh = "single",
  pseudo_cf_whole_oob = "whole_oob",
  pseudo_cf_whole_scf = "whole_scf",
  pseudo_cf_cvps_scf = "cvps_scf",
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob = "whole_oob",
  pseudo_dr_whole_scf = "whole_scf",
  pseudo_dr_cvps_scf = "cvps_scf",
  sl_t_whole = "whole",
  sl_t_cvps = "cvps",
  sl_t_split = "split",
  sl_dr_whole = "whole",
  sl_dr_cvps = "cvps",
  # the RSF outcome model fits (Y, D), so the whole/cvps pseudo-value factor
  # has nothing to act on - these arms vary the fitting only
  rsf_dr_oob = "oob",
  rsf_dr_scf = "scf",
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob_semi = "semi",
  sl_dr_whole_semi = "semi",
  rsf_dr_oob_semi = "semi"
)
variant_levels <- c(
  "single",
  "whole_oob",
  "whole_scf",
  "cvps_scf",
  "oob",
  "scf",
  "whole",
  "cvps",
  "split",
  "semi"
)
variant_labels <- c(
  single = "(single arm)",
  whole_oob = "Whole-sample, OOB",
  whole_scf = "Whole-sample, single CF",
  cvps_scf = "Crossfit PV, single CF",
  oob = "OOB",
  scf = "Single CF",
  whole = "Whole-sample PV",
  cvps = "Crossfit PV",
  split = "Split PV",
  semi = "Semi-oracle (e = 0.5)"
)

# tidy up
metrics_all <- metrics %>%
  mutate(
    family = factor(
      recode(framework, !!!framework_family),
      levels = family_levels
    ),
    variant = recode(framework, !!!framework_variant),
    variant = factor(
      recode(variant, !!!variant_labels),
      levels = unname(variant_labels[variant_levels])
    ),
    scenario = factor(
      scenario,
      levels = names(scenario_labels) %>% as.integer(),
      labels = unname(scenario_labels)
    ),
    censoring = factor(
      censoring,
      levels = c(TRUE, FALSE),
      labels = c("Censored", "Uncensored")
    ),
    target = factor(target, levels = c("Event 1", "Event 2", "Combined"))
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

# remove boring bits
metrics_all <- metrics_all %>%
  # remove CSH stuff for conference presentations
  #filter(!(family %in% c("CSF (cause-specific)", "IPW", "T: SL on PV"))) %>%
  # remove combined event
  filter(target != "Combined") %>%
  # remove superfluous crossfitting variants
  # filter(
  #   !(variant %in%
  #     c(
  #       "Split PV",
  #       "Whole-sample PV",
  #       "Whole-sample, OOB",
  #       "Whole-sample, single CF"
  #     ))
  # ) %>%
  droplevels()

# every section but "Sensitivity analysis" is the primary analysis, rho = 0.5
metrics <- filter(metrics_all, rho == 0.5)

# per (scenario, censoring, target, family, variant) summaries
#
# mcse denominator is sqrt(sum(!is.na(x))), matching the non-NA count of that
# column - not sqrt(n()), the whole group's row count regardless of NAs.
# corr/spearman/c_stat are genuinely NA for some Event 1 cells (zero-variance
# truth in scenario 5's ipw/csf_cs arms - see the correlation section below),
# so those columns are the most exposed.
metrics_summary <- metrics %>%
  group_by(scenario, censoring, target, family, variant) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_bias = mean(bias, na.rm = T),
    mcse_bias = sd(bias, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(bias))),
    mean_ate_bias = mean(ate_bias, na.rm = T),
    mcse_ate_bias = sd(ate_bias, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(ate_bias))),
    mean_rel_ate_bias = mean(rel_ate_bias, na.rm = T),
    mcse_rel_ate_bias = sd(rel_ate_bias, na.rm = T) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(rel_ate_bias))),
    mean_rel_bias_cate = mean(rel_bias_cate, na.rm = T),
    mcse_rel_bias_cate = sd(rel_bias_cate, na.rm = T) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(rel_bias_cate))),
    mean_mse = mean(mse, na.rm = T),
    mcse_mse = sd(mse, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(mse))),
    mean_rmse = mean(rmse, na.rm = T),
    mcse_rmse = sd(rmse, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(rmse))),
    mean_mae = mean(mae, na.rm = T),
    mcse_mae = sd(mae, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(mae))),
    mean_corr = mean(corr, na.rm = T),
    mcse_corr = sd(corr, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(corr))),
    mean_spearman = mean(spearman, na.rm = T),
    mcse_spearman = sd(spearman, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(spearman))),
    mean_sign_acc = mean(sign_acc, na.rm = T),
    mcse_sign_acc = sd(sign_acc, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(sign_acc))),
    mean_c_stat = mean(c_stat, na.rm = T),
    mcse_c_stat = sd(c_stat, na.rm = T) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(c_stat))),
    mean_n_na = mean(n_na, na.rm = T),
    total_n_na = sum(n_na, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Results coverage

The array job set is 14,000 runs (2 ρ x 7 scenarios x 2 censoring settings x
500 runs); `competing_risk/README.md` documents known partial-failure routes,
so this table is worth checking before reading anything else below.

```{r completeness-table}
completeness <- metrics_all %>%
  group_by(rho, scenario, censoring) %>%
  summarise(
    n_runs = n_distinct(run),
    n_frameworks = n_distinct(family, variant),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(rho, scenario, censoring)

kable(
  completeness,
  col.names = c("ρ", "Scenario", "Censoring", "Runs collected", "Arms present")
)
```

```{r forest-helpers, include=FALSE}
# helper: forest-style summary plot - one row per arm down y, grouped into a
# row of panels per family (strip on the left), the metric along x, a column
# per scenario. x is free per scenario column but shared down it, so arms
# compare within a scenario. Replaced the old family-on-x layout, which put
# ~500 dodged marks in one figure and coloured by variant, whose meaning
# changed from family to family. Error bars are 95% CIs (mean +/- qnorm(1 -
# alpha/2) x MCSE) - see R/figures.R's point_range_plot() (its alpha doc) for
# why this isn't a raw +/- 1x MCSE. Semi-oracle arms are dropped: they get
# their own section, as paired differences against their production arms.
# vline = NA draws no reference line.
forest_plot <- function(df, mean_col, mcse_col, xlab, title, vline = 0,
                        alpha = 0.05) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  single <- variant_labels[["single"]]
  semi <- variant_labels[["semi"]]
  arm_levels <- c("", setdiff(levels(df$variant), c(single, semi)))
  p <- df %>%
    filter(variant != semi) %>%
    mutate(
      est = .data[[mean_col]],
      lo = est - z * .data[[mcse_col]],
      hi = est + z * .data[[mcse_col]],
      # single-arm families: the family strip already names the arm
      arm = if_else(variant == single, "", as.character(variant)),
      arm = factor(arm, levels = rev(arm_levels))
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = est, xmin = lo, xmax = hi, y = arm, colour = family))
  if (!is.na(vline)) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = vline, linetype = "dashed")
  }
  p +
    geom_linerange(linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_grid(
      rows = vars(family),
      cols = vars(scenario),
      scales = "free",
      space = "free_y",
      switch = "y"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
    # drop = FALSE keeps each family's colour fixed across figures that
    # carry only some of the families (the semi-oracle section)
    scale_colour_paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe", drop = FALSE,
                             guide = "none") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      strip.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
      # family strips read as row labels, so no box around them
      strip.background.y = element_blank(),
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      panel.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "lines"),
      # room between scenario columns so edge tick labels don't collide
      panel.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "lines")
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = NULL)
}

# the views every metric is shown in, one tab each: target x censoring,
# censored first (the setting the trial data will have)
forest_views <- tibble(
  censoring = c("Censored", "Censored", "Uncensored", "Uncensored"),
  target = c("Event 1", "Event 2", "Event 1", "Event 2"),
  tab = c("Event 1", "Event 2", "Event 1, uncensored", "Event 2, uncensored"),
  slug = c("event1_censored", "event2_censored", "event1_uncensored",
           "event2_uncensored")
)

# writes a nested Quarto tabset - call it from a results="asis" chunk. One
# outer tab per spec (a metric), each holding a forest_plot() per
# forest_views row. A spec is a list of: tab, mean, mcse, xlab, title, and
# optionally vline (default 0, NA for none), data (in place of `df`, for
# per-metric long tables like the paired differences) and save (a file stem:
# each view is written to figdir as <save>_<slug>.png)
metric_tabs <- function(specs, df = NULL) {
  cat("::::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (s in specs) {
    d <- if (is.null(s$data)) df else s$data
    vline <- if (is.null(s$vline)) 0 else s$vline
    # every cat() below leads with blank lines: knitr drops the newlines that
    # follow a printed plot, which glues the next heading or fence onto the
    # image line and breaks the tabset
    cat("\n\n###", s$tab, "\n\n")
    cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(forest_views))) {
      v <- forest_views[i, ]
      p <- forest_plot(
        filter(d, censoring == v$censoring, target == v$target),
        s$mean,
        s$mcse,
        s$xlab,
        paste0(s$title, ": ", v$tab),
        vline = vline
      )
      cat("\n\n####", v$tab, "\n\n")
      print(p)
      if (!is.null(s$save)) {
        ggsave(paste0(s$save, "_", v$slug, ".png"), plot = p, path = figdir,
               height = 20, width = 30, units = "cm")
      }
    }
    cat("\n\n:::\n\n")
  }
  cat("\n\n:::::\n\n")
}
```

## Bias

Average bias in the estimated CATE (estimate minus truth), against each
target's own truth column, plus the ATE and relative versions. `rel_ate_bias`
is the parameter-level relative bias (ATE bias divided by the true ATE);
`rel_bias_cate` is the per-unit version, `(est - true) / true` averaged over
units (undefined and set to `NA` wherever the true CATE is exactly 0 for a
unit — see `R/metrics.R::cate_metrics()`).

```{r bias-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
metric_tabs(
  list(
    list(tab = "CATE bias", mean = "mean_bias", mcse = "mcse_bias",
         xlab = "Mean bias", title = "Mean bias in CATE estimates",
         save = "surv_bias"),
    list(tab = "ATE bias", mean = "mean_ate_bias", mcse = "mcse_ate_bias",
         xlab = "Mean ATE bias", title = "Mean bias in the ATE",
         save = "surv_ate_bias"),
    list(tab = "Relative ATE bias", mean = "mean_rel_ate_bias",
         mcse = "mcse_rel_ate_bias", xlab = "Mean relative ATE bias",
         title = "Mean relative bias in the ATE", save = "surv_rel_ate_bias"),
    list(tab = "Relative CATE bias", mean = "mean_rel_bias_cate",
         mcse = "mcse_rel_bias_cate", xlab = "Mean relative CATE bias",
         title = "Mean relative bias in the CATE", save = "surv_rel_bias_cate")
  ),
  metrics_summary
)
```

## Error in the CATE estimates

The headline metric is the error of the estimated CATE against the known
truth. RMSE (`sqrt(mse)`) is shown first: it ranks arms the same way as MSE
but on the outcome's own scale. MAE is a robustness check, less sensitive to
outlying runs. There is no reference line at 0 here, because 0 is a floor,
not a target, and including it would compress the differences between arms.

```{r error-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
metric_tabs(
  list(
    list(tab = "RMSE", mean = "mean_rmse", mcse = "mcse_rmse",
         xlab = "Mean RMSE", title = "Mean RMSE of CATE estimates",
         vline = NA, save = "surv_rmse"),
    list(tab = "MSE", mean = "mean_mse", mcse = "mcse_mse",
         xlab = "Mean MSE", title = "Mean MSE of CATE estimates",
         vline = NA, save = "surv_mse"),
    list(tab = "MAE", mean = "mean_mae", mcse = "mcse_mae",
         xlab = "Mean MAE", title = "Mean MAE of CATE estimates",
         vline = NA, save = "surv_mae")
  ),
  metrics_summary
)
```

## Ranking the true CATE

How well each arm orders units by their true CATE:

- **C-statistic**: `(Kendall's tau_b + 1) / 2`, a rank-concordance measure
  equivalent to Harrell's C for a continuous outcome; 0.5 (dashed) is chance.
- **Correlation**: Pearson correlation between estimated and true CATEs.
- **Spearman**: rank correlation, less sensitive to outlying CATE estimates
  and non-linear-but-monotone miscalibration.
- **Sign accuracy**: proportion of units where the estimated CATE has the
  correct sign; 0.5 (dashed) is chance.

Scenario 1 is included: its CATE varies with X1 and X2 (SD about 0.1 days),
so these are defined there, if small and noisy. `surv_metrics.R` computes
them rather than taking `cate_metrics()`'s null-scenario 0. Also see the
scenario-5 note above: the `ipw`/`csf_cs` Event 1 cells there are genuine `NA`
(zero-variance truth), dropped by `na.rm = TRUE` rather than shown as 0.

```{r ranking-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
metric_tabs(
  list(
    list(tab = "C-statistic", mean = "mean_c_stat", mcse = "mcse_c_stat",
         xlab = "Mean C-statistic", title = "Mean C-statistic", vline = 0.5),
    list(tab = "Correlation", mean = "mean_corr", mcse = "mcse_corr",
         xlab = "Mean correlation",
         title = "Mean correlation with the true CATE"),
    list(tab = "Spearman", mean = "mean_spearman", mcse = "mcse_spearman",
         xlab = "Mean Spearman correlation",
         title = "Mean Spearman correlation with the true CATE"),
    list(tab = "Sign accuracy", mean = "mean_sign_acc",
         mcse = "mcse_sign_acc", xlab = "Mean proportion correct sign",
         title = "Mean sign accuracy", vline = 0.5)
  ),
  metrics_summary
)
```

## Cost of estimating the propensity

Each of the three DR families has a semi-oracle twin (`*_semi`). It uses
the same fitted outcome models but puts the true propensity, 0.5, into the
DR pseudo-outcome in place of the estimated one. The stage-2 regression is
refit on that pseudo-outcome (`surv_models.R`). Comparing an arm with its
twin on the same run isolates what estimating the propensity does, plus
stage-2 fitting noise.

These are paired differences: per run, production minus semi-oracle, then
averaged, with MCSE = sd(diff) / √pairs. A positive MSE difference means
estimating the propensity costs accuracy. A positive correlation or
C-statistic difference means it helps. Primary analysis only (ρ = 0.5).

```{r semi-paired}
# production arm -> its semi-oracle twin
semi_pairs <- c(
  pseudo_dr_whole_oob = "pseudo_dr_whole_oob_semi",
  sl_dr_whole = "sl_dr_whole_semi",
  rsf_dr_oob = "rsf_dr_oob_semi"
)

paired_semi <- metrics %>%
  filter(framework %in% c(names(semi_pairs), semi_pairs)) %>%
  mutate(
    arm_type = if_else(framework %in% semi_pairs, "semi", "prod"),
    base = if_else(
      arm_type == "semi",
      names(semi_pairs)[match(framework, semi_pairs)],
      framework
    ),
    # label each pair by its production arm
    variant = factor(
      unname(variant_labels[framework_variant[base]]),
      levels = levels(metrics$variant)
    )
  ) %>%
  select(scenario, censoring, target, family, variant, arm_type, run,
         mse, corr, c_stat) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mse, corr, c_stat), names_to = "metric") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = arm_type, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = prod - semi) %>%
  group_by(metric, scenario, censoring, target, family, variant) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    mcse_diff = sd(diff, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(diff))),
    pairs = sum(!is.na(diff)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r semi-plots, results="asis", fig.height=3.5}
metric_tabs(list(
  list(tab = "MSE", data = filter(paired_semi, metric == "mse"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff", xlab = "MSE difference",
       title = "Paired difference in MSE, estimated − true propensity",
       save = "surv_semi_mse_diff"),
  list(tab = "Correlation", data = filter(paired_semi, metric == "corr"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff",
       xlab = "Correlation difference",
       title = "Paired difference in correlation, estimated − true propensity"),
  list(tab = "C-statistic", data = filter(paired_semi, metric == "c_stat"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff",
       xlab = "C-statistic difference",
       title = "Paired difference in C-statistic, estimated − true propensity")
))
```

## Missing estimates

`n_na` is a data-quality diagnostic, not a performance metric: the count of
`NA` CATE estimates within a run (see `competing_risk/README.md`'s "Known
issues" for the failure routes that produce these). Mostly zero, so shown as
a table rather than a distribution plot; only cells with at least one
missing estimate are listed.

```{r na-table}
na_table <- metrics_summary %>%
  select(
    scenario,
    censoring,
    target,
    family,
    variant,
    mean_n_na,
    total_n_na
  ) %>%
  filter(total_n_na > 0) %>%
  arrange(scenario, censoring, target, family, variant)

if (nrow(na_table) > 0) {
  kable(
    na_table,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
      "Scenario",
      "Censoring",
      "Target",
      "Family",
      "Arm",
      "Mean NA count per run",
      "Total NA count"
    )
  )
} else {
  cat("No missing CATE estimates in any collected run.")
}
```

## Headline table

Arranged by scenario, censoring, target, and mean MSE (best arm first
within each cell).

```{r headline-table}
headline <- metrics_summary %>%
  select(

    target,

kable(

)
```

## Sensitivity analysis: independent covariates (ρ = 0)

Every section above is ρ = 0.5, where the modifier X3 is correlated with the
prognostic X1 and X2 (about 0.3–0.4) and with the noise X4, X5 and X01–X03, which become
partial proxies for it. At ρ = 0 all covariates are independent. The true
CATE function, the event mix and the scenarios' X3 separation barely move
between the two (`surv_dgm_check.R`; ADEMP "What the DGM implies"), so a
change here is the estimators' doing, not the truth's.

Each run is seeded by its run index alone, so run *r* at the two ρ shares W,
the copula's raw normals, the categorical noise and the event-time uniforms.
The differences below are therefore paired: per run, ρ = 0 minus ρ = 0.5 (the
sensitivity analysis minus the primary), then averaged, with MCSE =
sd(diff) / √pairs (as `sample_size/`). A positive MSE difference
means that arm does worse with independent covariates than in the primary
analysis; a positive correlation or C-statistic difference means it does
better.

```{r sens-paired}
paired_rho <- metrics_all %>%
  select(rho, scenario, censoring, target, family, variant, run,
         mse, corr, c_stat) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(mse, corr, c_stat), names_to = "metric") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rho, values_from = value, names_prefix = "rho_") %>%
  mutate(diff = rho_0 - rho_0.5) %>%
  group_by(metric, scenario, censoring, target, family, variant) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_diff = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
    mcse_diff = sd(diff, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(diff))),
    pairs = sum(!is.na(diff)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r sens-plots, results="asis", fig.height=8}
metric_tabs(list(
  list(tab = "MSE", data = filter(paired_rho, metric == "mse"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff", xlab = "MSE difference",
       title = "Paired difference in MSE, ρ = 0 − ρ = 0.5",
       save = "surv_rho_mse_diff"),
  list(tab = "Correlation", data = filter(paired_rho, metric == "corr"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff",
       xlab = "Correlation difference",
       title = "Paired difference in correlation with the true CATE, ρ = 0 − ρ = 0.5"),
  list(tab = "C-statistic", data = filter(paired_rho, metric == "c_stat"),
       mean = "mean_diff", mcse = "mcse_diff",
       xlab = "C-statistic difference",
       title = "Paired difference in C-statistic, ρ = 0 − ρ = 0.5")
))
```
